item.title: reports: per-currency totals
item.brief: Operator instruction (verbatim): reports (Python) reads that CSV on stdin and prints per-account totals. It must now total per account and currency: header account,currency,total_cents, rows sorted by account then currency. CSV from the old ledger (no currency column) still works and counts as USD. A malformed currency code in the input makes reports.py print an error to stderr and exit with status 2. Keep the existing tests passing (python3 -m unittest), add tests for the new behaviour, update the README, and commit. Follow the shared contract exactly. Another member changes the ledger repo to emit the new four-column CSV; build against the contract.

pr.body: Approach: reports.py groups totals by (account, currency). currency_of() reads the optional currency column (default USD) and fullmatches [A-Z]{3}; a MalformedCurrency error maps to stderr and exit 2 in main(). render() writes the new header and sorted rows. Key files: reports.py, test_reports.py, README.md. Tests: existing test kept; new tests cover per-currency totals, legacy input as USD, and malformed codes (usd, US, USDX, U5D, empty, leading space) exiting 2 with empty stdout. Results: 4 tests OK. Review: one reviewer, pass, no blocking findings. Follow-ups (non-blocking): short-row message says 'None' instead of naming the row; line number for quoted embedded newlines is the record end; no CRLF or short-row tests. Assumption: an empty currency cell in a file that has the column is malformed. Callers parsing the old two-column output must change.
pr.summary: made reports total per account and currency. now: header account,currency,total_cents, sorted by account then currency; missing currency column counts as USD; malformed currency exits 2. before: account,total_cents only, no currency handling.

item.title: ledger: currency column
item.brief: Operator instruction (verbatim): Our books now hold more than one currency. Two repositories need to change together. ledger (Rust) converts a TSV of transactions on stdin into CSV on stdout. Input lines may now carry a fourth column, the ISO 4217 currency code (exactly three uppercase ASCII letters, e.g. EUR); when it is missing the currency is USD. The CSV header becomes date,account,amount_cents,currency and every row gets the currency. A malformed currency code must make ledger print an error naming the line number to stderr and exit with status 2 (other input errors keep exiting with status 1). Keep the existing tests passing (cargo test), add tests for the new behaviour, update the README, and commit. Follow the shared contract exactly.

state.summary:
ledger: currency column implemented and committed on archon/hzqbkk48-ledger-currency-column as 55bd23c (tree 50f4a68), based on cef4446. Input lines accept an optional fourth column currency (three uppercase ASCII letters, trimmed like the other columns); missing means USD. Output header is date,account,amount_cents,currency and every row carries its currency. A malformed currency exits 2 with "line N: bad currency ..." on stderr; other input errors still exit 1. parse_line now returns a ParseError enum (Malformed / BadCurrency) with exit_status(). README updated. Checks: cargo fmt --check clean; cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; cargo test: 9 integration tests pass (the earlier -900 expectation was my test error and was corrected). Review: one reviewer (agt_01M7WG53FJKMCH9SM1VNXXZRVP) passed the head with no blocking findings. Open non-blocking items: the currency field is trimmed, so " EUR" is accepted, which is a deliberate choice to match the other columns and handle CRLF; the "US " test case does not exercise trailing-space rejection; a trailing tab with an empty 4th column exits 2 rather than defaulting to USD. Nothing is left running. Not pushed.
